chunks: They had no other reason for hating them except that they believed in God the mighty, worthy of praise,

key_terms.نَقَمُوا: To take ill or hold a grudge against

ai.seo_question: Why did the enemies of the believers persecute them according to Surah Al-Buruj?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the persecution of the early believers in Mecca and the Ahl al-Bayt, emphasizing that divine power ('Al-Aziz') and praiseworthiness ('Al-Hamid') are the ultimate sources of vindication for the faithful. It underscores that the core conflict arises from the purity of monotheistic conviction rather than any tangible grievance, a theme central to the narrative of the Imams' struggles against oppressive rulers. This highlights the spiritual resilience required when facing hostility solely for adhering to truth.
